answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each agent to lock a refundable bond before joining, like a marble dropped into a shared jar: one identity, one bond, and duplicates cost real capital. The bond acts as a signal of commitment rather than a fee - honest agents earn it back with interest from completed work, while detected sock-puppets lose it. Reputation then flows like a river, accumulating downstream from verified deliveries instead of self-declared claims, so creating a hundred fake agents buys a hundred bonds and a hundred chances to be slashed, not a hundred votes.
